x: Makkhali Gosala is the founder/leader of the Ajivika sect in the books (PMF, Singhania); Buddhist texts name Nanda Vaccha and Kisa Sankicca as earlier teachers, but Gosala is the answer taught.

dispute: Old app key: Nanda Vachcha (a predecessor in Buddhist tradition). Books and exam keys: Makkhali Gosala (PMF Art & Culture 05 p.104).

x: Gandhi founded his Satyagraha Ashram on 25 May 1915 at Kochrab, Ahmedabad, the start usually given for the Sabarmati Ashram; it moved to the Sabarmati bank on 17 June 1917.
source: https://www.mkgandhi.org/museum/Sabarmati.htm (founded 25 May 1915 at Kochrab; shifted to Sabarmati 17 June 1917)
dispute: Most keys: 1915-16 (founding at Kochrab, 25 May 1915). Strictly the ashram moved to the Sabarmati bank on 17 June 1917 (mkgandhi.org).

x: Gandhi's first movement after returning to India was Champaran (1917), against the forced tinkathia indigo cultivation that planters imposed on tenants – the 'contract farming' of the options. The anti-indenture ('coolie') campaign is the tempting distractor.
source: Spectrum Modern India p.316, p.349 (Champaran 1917 first civil disobedience, tinkathia); https://testbook.com/question-answer/after-return-to-india-the-first-movement-led-by-m--69e65ad9e6c0a3df6ed1335a (key: Contract farming)
dispute: Key / books: Contract farming (Champaran 1917). Strictly Gandhi's campaign against indentured coolie emigration (1915-17) came earlier.

x: Books and keys link the 'Himalayan blunder' to the withdrawal of Non-Cooperation after Chauri Chaura (1922). Gandhi in fact used the phrase about the Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 (see the dispute line).
evidence: NextGen Rocket Indian History 02 p.54 (Chauri Chaura – NCM withdrawn)
dispute: Most books and keys: Chauri Chaura. Strictly: Gandhi's 'Himalayan blunder (miscalculation)' was his admission about launching the Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 before people were ready (PMF Modern History Part 4 p.138).
